official.deadline_note: The application period for International Master's Programmes starting in autumn 2027 runs from 5 to 19 January 2027. The tuition fee waiver is requested on the same application form, so the scholarship deadline is the application deadline; there is no separate scholarship window.
official.application_cycle: International Master's Programmes, autumn 2027 intake; application period 5 to 19 January 2027
official.status_note: The university states: 'The application period for studies starting in autumn 2027 is from 5 to 19 Jan 2027.' On the date checked the round had not yet opened.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The university states: 'University of Helsinki scholarship programme consists of tuition fee waivers, waiving the tuition fee for 50 % or 100 %. Please note that only very limited number of tuition fee waivers can be awarded and most of them cover 50 % of the tuition fee.' Published fees for Master's Programmes in English are 13,000, 15,000 and 18,000 EUR per academic year depending on the programme, and 13,000 EUR per academic year for the English-language bachelor's programmes. The university also states plainly that it does not offer scholarships to cover living expenses.
benefits: Tuition fee waiver of 50% or 100% of the programme tuition fee, with the majority of available waivers at 50%
The waiver covers two years and continues into the second study year if at least 55 ECTS were completed in the first year, subject to a progress check
Graduates of an English-language bachelor's programme who continue to a Helsinki master's receive a waiver automatically by GPA: 3.8/5 or above qualifies for 100%, and 3.4-3.7/5 qualifies for 50%
eligibility: Eligible for the Master's programme at the University of Helsinki
Liable for tuition fees: a citizen of a non-EU/EEA country who does not have permanent residence status in Finland
Meets the requirements for obtaining an entry visa and residence permit for Finland
Has obtained excellent results in previous studies and can prove this in the application
Students not liable to pay tuition fees, including EU/EEA citizens, cannot apply for the waiver
requirements: Apply for the tuition fee waiver with the same application form used to apply to the Master's programme
Submit all the required attachments with that application
Sign a scholarship agreement before the waiver comes into effect
Study full time and earn at least 55 ECTS per year to fulfil the requirements of the scholarship
documents: Master's programme application form, with the tuition fee waiver requested on it
Previous study records proving excellent academic results
The documents required by the individual master's programme
selection_criteria: Academic overall assessment of the degree application and the scholarship application
Previous academic performance and possible letters of motivation
The grounds presented by applicants in their grant applications
The University's and the programmes' strategic goals, which can also be taken into account
Some programmes may award only 50% waivers, and how waivers are distributed depends on each programme's scholarship policy and the size and level of its applicant batch
coverage: 50% or 100% of the tuition fee for two years, with most awards at 50%
No living costs; the university states it does not offer scholarships to cover living expenses
No travel costs are mentioned on the official page
With a 50% waiver the remaining tuition fee must still be paid before registration as an attending student
application_method: Find the Master's programme to apply to through the university's programme search
Read the instructions on how to apply to that programme and prepare the necessary attachments
Apply for a tuition fee waiver with the same application form used for the Master's programme
official.application_route: Request the waiver inside the master's application form itself; the result arrives with the acceptance e-mail and a scholarship agreement must then be signed.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of non-EU/EEA countries who do not have permanent residence status in Finland are liable to pay tuition fees and are the intended applicants. Citizens of the EU, EEA and Switzerland, holders of a permanent residence card, a long-term resident's EU residence permit, a residence permit based on temporary protection, an EU blue card, a Brexit right of residence, an EU family member's residence card, Erasmus Mundus scholars, exchange students and PhD students are not liable and cannot hold the waiver.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme is aimed specifically at students from outside the EU/EEA who are liable to pay tuition fees.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Available only to applicants to International Master's Programmes at the University of Helsinki. There are no tuition fee waivers for applicants to the English-language bachelor's degrees, although a bachelor's programme may award a Dean's award of 1,000 EUR to second and third year students on the basis of study performance.
official.duration: Two years. Students must study full time and earn at least 55 ECTS per year, and after the first study year the progress of studies is checked before the scholarship is continued.
official.description: The University of Helsinki scholarship programme consists of tuition fee waivers of 50% or 100% for excellent tuition fee-liable students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who want to complete a Master's programme. Only a very limited number of waivers exist and most cover 50%, and the university states that it does not offer scholarships to cover living expenses.
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition fee waiver, 50% or 100%, decided with the admission result

not_confirmed: required document list beyond 'previous study records' and 'documents required by the programme'
verification.notes: The university's own tuition fees and scholarship programme page was read in full, plus its apply-to-international-master's-programmes page for the autumn 2027 dates and application fee. The page still labels the two waiver categories 'for application round 2025-26', so the categories themselves are stated for the previous round although the structure and rules are otherwise current. The university publishes tuition fee tariffs rather than a single scholarship figure, so the amount fields are null.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate scholarship form: the waiver is requested on the master's application itself, which means the only deadline that matters is 19 January 2027 and there is no second chance to add it later. The realistic expectation is a 50% waiver, because the university says outright that most of the very few awards are 50% and that some programmes award nothing but 50%. Because the university also states that it offers no living-cost support, an applicant needs roughly 13,000 to 18,000 EUR of tuition plus living costs for two years funded from other sources even after a full waiver is unlikely to arrive.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants to a Helsinki International Master's Programme with an outstanding academic transcript who can prove excellent previous results and who can fund living costs independently.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your fee liability status before applying, because a student who is not liable for tuition fees cannot hold the waiver at all
Read the scholarship-relevant wording on your chosen programme's page, since distribution is decided programme by programme
Prepare the attachments the programme requires, because the fee waiver is judged on the same material as the degree application
Plan around the ECTS condition: the second year of the waiver depends on completing at least 55 ECTS in the first year
Budget for the one-time 100 euro national application fee unless a specific exemption applies, since there is no waiver for it
common_rejection_risks: Assuming a 100% waiver is the norm; the university states the majority of awards are 50%
Applying to a programme that in practice awards only 50% waivers or none at all in that round
Failing to prove excellent previous study results inside the application rather than promising them
Signing nothing after admission: the waiver only comes into effect once the scholarship agreement is signed
Dropping below 55 ECTS in the first study year and losing the second year of the waiver
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living expenses in full, since the university states it does not offer scholarships to cover them, plus the remaining tuition fee if awarded a 50% waiver, plus the compulsory Student Union HYY membership fee and the Finnish Student Health Service fee paid directly to Kela.
document_audit: The official page describes the required material only as 'previous study records' and 'the documents required by the master's programme', so the programme's own attachment list is the authoritative document checklist
If your residence or citizenship status changes during your studies you must inform the university, because losing fee liability also ends the scholarship

The university's admissions pages note that instructions were written for the round that closed 16 January 2026, so treat programme-level detail as provisional until the 2027 intake guidance is published
With a 50% waiver you still must pay the remaining tuition before registering as an attending student; only a 100% waiver removes that step
alerts: The waiver categories are still labelled 'for application round 2025-26' on the official page, so confirm the current round's terms when the January 2027 application opens
Providing false information in the scholarship application or cheating ends the right to the scholarship outright
A residence permit used to claim exemption must be valid on 1 August of the year the fee applies, and permit history is checked with the Finnish Migration Service
This award is easily confused with the small, separately administered University of Helsinki scholarships, which the university itself describes as relatively small in amount
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One application form covering both the master's programme and the waiver request, submitted 5 to 19 January 2027, with academic assessment by the programme and the waiver result delivered inside the official acceptance e-mail, followed by signing a scholarship agreement.
